I001.summary_en: Classifies student mental health using a psycholinguistic dataset, comparing Logistic/Linear Regression, SVM, Decision Tree and Random Forest. The linear regression classifier achieved the highest accuracy (65%).

I002.best_result: Random Forest regression R² = 1; Logistic Regression accuracy 0.99
I002.summary_en: Predicts the emotional well-being of 719 undergraduate students from 10 Likert-scale questionnaires using regression, classification and clustering (K-Means, hierarchical, DBSCAN). Random Forest regression reached R² = 1 and Logistic Regression 0.99 accuracy; clustering revealed compact well-being profiles.

I003.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; analytical method and data not described
I003.summary_en: Describes a big data-driven mental health assessment model for college students combining a questionnaire (family life, academic performance, peer relations) with an unspecified set of algorithms. No data, method details or results are reported.

I004.summary_en: Proposes a mental health prediction model for college students that mines association rules with FP-Growth over multi-source data (behavior, learning performance, social relations) and predicts risk with XGBoost. It claims high accuracy and speed without reporting data or metrics.

I005.summary_en: Analyzes the mental health of 379 vocational college students in Shenzhen with quantitative assessment tools across cognitive, emotional, personality and behavioral dimensions. 55.94% showed good mental health and 19.53% depressive tendencies; emotional state correlated with social support (r = 0.68), and a warning index model was built.

I006.screening_reason: No data analytics applied; essay on mental health education strategy
I006.summary_en: Discusses the impact of the internet on vocational college students' mental health and proposes mental health education strategies. No data analysis is performed.

I007.summary_en: Analyzes multi-year 16PF evaluation data of college students with statistical analysis in Stata to explore gender differences in mental health. It finds clear gender differences in mental health.

I008.summary_en: Designs a mental health assessment system for college students based on an improved Apriori algorithm, validated through simulation tests. It claims improved precision and efficiency without reporting figures.

I009.summary_en: Proposes a big data-based early warning and intervention system for college students' mental health. No data, specific method or results are reported.

I010.summary_en: Mines large-scale mental health data from a psychological evaluation system with the Apriori algorithm to build a weighted association-rule risk prediction model for college students. It identifies associations among study time, social activities and sleep time.

I011.summary_en: Uses unspecified machine learning algorithms to analyze college students' mental health data and build a classification model for screening sub-healthy students. No data or results are reported.

I012.summary_en: Builds a mental health risk early warning system for college students based on Apriori data mining. It reports 96.57% accuracy and AUC 0.9678 in dataset testing, outperforming common systems, without describing the dataset.

I013.summary_en: Designs a data mining platform (SQL Server, Visual Basic) that preprocesses college students' psychological evaluation data and applies Apriori association rules. The model reveals relationships between multiple attributes and psychological symptoms.

I014.summary_en: Examines the influence of personality traits on emotional well-being in 123 postgraduate students using 16 Personalities test responses processed with NLP and sentiment analysis. Extraversion and conscientiousness were associated with positive affect and neuroticism with stress and anxiety; female students reported more anxiety and stress.

I015.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; outcome is mainly personality classification
I015.summary_en: Proposes a psychological prediction algorithm for college students based on internet data mining, using personal information from the school website and Big Five personality scores to classify students as good or bad. No method details or results are reported.

I016.summary_en: Applies unspecified machine learning algorithms to large-scale data on college students' mental health to predict status and identify factors. Academic stress and social interaction correlated with mental health, with differences by gender, academic year and background; no metrics are reported.

I017.summary_en: Applies K-means clustering to college students' mental health evaluation data and assesses clustering quality with the silhouette coefficient. Clusters differed significantly in anxiety and depression indicators and were stable.

I018.summary_en: Proposes a data analysis model based on the Apriori algorithm applied to mental health questionnaire data of college students. It identifies associations between psychological problems and behavioral characteristics to support personalized interventions.

I019.screening_reason: Review of digital interventions in general; ML is only one category
I019.summary_en: Systematic literature review (PRISMA) of 96 studies on technology-driven strategies for university students' emotional well-being, including machine learning-based solutions. It reports symptom reduction and identifies five success factors such as personalization and accessibility.

I020.summary_en: Proposes a platform combining questionnaire assessments with visual analysis and unspecified machine learning techniques for early detection of mental health issues in Indian students. It reports thematic clusters of emotional states without metrics.

I021.summary_en: Develops an intelligent perception model with a three-tier architecture to detect college students' psychological abnormalities from educational big data using classification and association rule mining. No data or metrics are reported.

I022.summary_en: Aims to build a machine learning tool to detect whether school children are happy or sad as an indicator of emotional well-being. No data, specific method or results are reported.

I023.summary_en: Designs a data mining-based early warning model for college students' psychological problems using quantified behavioral characteristics and early warning rules. No specific algorithm or results are reported.

I024.screening_reason: Abstract does not describe the analytical method; focus on mental health education system
I024.summary_en: Discusses a college mental health education system based on data mining technology. It reports that 13.5% of students were severely depressed and 20.1% severely anxious, without describing data or method.

I025.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; clustering targets research group ability rather than mental health
I025.summary_en: Designs a monitoring platform for college mental health education based on internet trace data collected with web crawlers and PAM clustering. The abstract mixes research-group ability evaluation with mental health and reports no results.

I026.summary_en: Predicts depression levels in undergraduate students in blended learning from questionnaires covering psychological, behavioral, academic and demographic indicators, using Logistic Regression, Random Forest and KNN. Logistic Regression performed best (accuracy 0.92, F1 0.91); procrastination, task-accuracy concerns and low self-confidence were key predictors.

I027.summary_en: Builds a Hadoop-based mental health database for college students from poverty-stricken families using K-means clustering and C4.5 decision trees for recognition and early warning. No data or results are reported.

I028.summary_en: Proposes a mental health evaluation data model for college students drawing on MOOC learning behavior tables, with clustering, social network mining and language analysis. No data or results are reported.

I029.summary_en: Evaluates a data-driven AI music therapy framework in a 12-week intervention with 500 university students using self-report scales, physiological signals and music interaction logs. The intervention group showed a 25% greater reduction in stress and a 16% greater increase in positive affect than controls.

I030.screening_reason: Optimization algorithm (branch and bound) rather than data analytics; data and results not described
I030.summary_en: Explores the use of the branch and bound algorithm to support mental health assessment and intervention decisions for college students. Data and results are not described.

I031.summary_en: Studies an intelligent prediction model of college students' mental health based on cluster analysis, grouping students and analyzing factors associated with psychological problems. It reports a gender difference in decisiveness (t = 9.55) but no data description or predictive metrics.

I032.screening_reason: Mainly an essay on mental health education; analytical method not described
I032.summary_en: Discusses opportunities of big data for university mental health education and designs a platform that uses big data analysis to assess students' mental health status. No data, method or results are described.

I033.screening_reason: No data analytics applied; proposals for peer-assistance psychological education
I033.summary_en: Proposes course content and teaching methods for peer mutual-aid psychological education of college students in the we-media era, including dynamic psychological archives. No data analysis is performed.

I034.summary_en: Builds a C4.5 decision tree model to predict college students' psychological problems and uses clustering to identify groups at risk of anxiety and depression. No data or metrics are reported.

I035.summary_en: Designs an intelligent platform that collects personal information, learning behavior and social media activity to detect students' anxiety, depression and stress and provide warnings and support. No specific algorithm, data or results are reported.

I036.best_result: False positive and false negative rates ≤ 1%
I036.summary_en: Applies heuristic text clustering to large-scale internet text to build an evaluation index system (emotional adjustment, learning, life and career influence) for college students' mental health. It reports false positive and false negative rates below 1% without describing the dataset.

I037.summary_en: Builds a mental health early warning system for college students based on system dynamics and tests it. Data classification accuracy was mostly 98–99%, without describing data or classification method.

I038.screening_reason: Bibliometric analysis of the literature, not analysis of student data
I038.summary_en: Bibliometric analysis of CSSCI literature on Chinese college students' mental health with co-occurrence visualization and keyword clustering (Louvain). Publications show a downward trend, with depression as a research hotspot and three keyword clusters.

I039.screening_reason: Outcome is internet use behavior and academic performance, not mental health
I039.summary_en: Proposes a Behavioral Characteristics Extraction Model using clustering of campus network behavior of undergraduates. It identifies 400 heavy internet users in four categories, with an impact on academic performance.

I040.summary_en: Builds a binary classifier of health versus sub-health status from 870 mental health survey records, selecting five features by chi-square test and training an SVM with Gaussian kernel and Bayesian optimization. The SVM reached 94.29% test accuracy, 5.72–17.15 points above random forest, decision tree and other models.

I041.summary_en: Analyzes data from 11,943 college students on 12 factors (e.g., somatization, obsessive-compulsive symptoms, interpersonal relationships) with descriptive statistics and K-means clustering. The best clustering was obtained with k = 4.

I042.screening_reason: Focus on physical fitness testing, not mental health
I042.summary_en: Explores the use of big data and SPSS statistical analysis of college students' physical fitness test data to design exercise programs. No mental health outcome is analyzed.

I043.summary_en: Compares ten machine learning algorithms on mental health screening records of students at a Chinese university (2017–2019) to select an optimal model and builds a prototype early warning system. Algorithms and results are not reported.

I044.screening_reason: Focus on physical fitness monitoring, not mental health
I044.summary_en: Studies a big data-based physical fitness monitoring system for Chinese students using data mining algorithms. The excellence rate was 46.7% for freshmen and 27.3% for juniors.

I045.screening_reason: Student management information platform; not about mental health; incoherent abstract
I045.summary_en: Describes a student management information platform for second-classroom activities with big data analysis and an encoder-based stability framework. The abstract is incoherent and does not address mental health.

I046.screening_reason: Focus on sports data analysis, not mental health
I046.summary_en: Describes the principles and application of data mining to university sports data. No mental health outcome, data or results are reported.

I047.screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance in relation to mental health
I047.summary_en: Analyzes the relationships among academic performance, mental health profiles and gender in 313 vocational college students with 14 methods, from Naive Bayes and SVM to BiLSTM and temporal CNN. It finds a robust association between mental health and achievement, with gender having negligible influence on psychological assessments.

I048.screening_reason: Information systems for mental health education; no analytical method described
I048.summary_en: Describes a psychological file management system and a mental health teaching platform for college students, with big data analysis used to update assessment norms. No data analysis method or results are reported.

I049.summary_en: Proposes an ensemble of gated recurrent and feed-forward networks (FFDN) to assess college students' psychological well-being from behavioral and emotional cues using Kaggle datasets. It outperforms other deep learning models with 97.3% accuracy and 96.6% F1.

I050.summary_en: Proposes a dynamic machine learning-based psychological health assessment system for college students using self-reported measures, academic performance and social interactions. No specific algorithm, data or results are reported.

I051.summary_en: Describes an algorithm-driven early warning and intervention system that monitors social interactions, academic performance and behavioral changes of college students from campus and digital sources. It claims improved mental health service delivery without data or metrics.

I052.summary_en: Proposes a multi-model ensemble approach to identify university students susceptible to mental health issues from demographic, academic and social characteristics. No data or results are reported.

I053.summary_en: Uses multi-source behavioral data and a convolutional neural network, compared with several classifiers, to identify college students' mental health problems. It reports improved identification without metrics.

I054.summary_en: Analyzes TikTok big data on Chinese university students' mental health crisis through visual knowledge maps, emotion models and keyword analysis. It describes the current situation and trends without quantitative results.

I055.summary_en: Presents WellScan, a framework based on Maslow's hierarchy and PERMA that uses Random Forest and Gradient Boosting to predict K-12 students at risk of wellbeing problems. A pilot with 400 students showed a strong correlation between higher wellbeing and academic performance.

I056.summary_en: Clusters the mental health of engineering students at Universitas Islam Lamongan with k-means using questionnaires and psychological tests (857 records). Two clusters (depressed and normal) emerged; weekly study hours strongly influenced mental health, averaging 40 hours in the depressed group.

I057.screening_reason: Focus on physical education learning outcomes, not mental health
I057.summary_en: Proposes a data mining system to analyze university students' physical education learning using PE scores, sports participation and physical health data. No mental health outcome is analyzed.

I058.summary_en: Examines college students' stress related to exams, recruitment and internet use with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Hist Gradient Boosting and KNN. Decision Tree achieved the highest accuracy (91%), followed by RF and LR (90%); the dataset is not described.

I059.summary_en: Applies fuzzy C-means clustering to UPI mental health test data of college students to identify groups and relationships among traits such as anxiety, introversion and emotional stability. It reports that 80% of students had normal mental health and males showed more prominent problems.

I060.summary_en: Screens depression in college students from non-clinical information (demographics, physical health, relationships, university life) with a machine learning approach and resampling for class imbalance. Average accuracy across classes reached 0.66.

I061.summary_en: Plans to classify higher education students into stress, depression and anxiety categories using SVM, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree and a neural network to identify the best algorithm per condition. No results are reported.

I062.summary_en: Detects mental disorders in students of a Mexican medical school from online PHQ-9 questionnaire data using machine learning, and uses regression to relate items to dropout ideation. The model achieved AUC 0.69, and PHQ-9 item 6 was the strongest predictor of dropout ideation.

I063.summary_en: Applies Fuzzy C-Means clustering to mental health data of art students to extract information and build a management model for prevention and counseling. No data details or results are reported.

I064.summary_en: Proposes a hybrid model combining Decision Trees, Gradient Boosting, SVM and Logistic Regression for automated assessment of stress, anxiety and depression in college students. It reports 96.4% accuracy and 96.0% F1 without describing the dataset.

I065.screening_reason: System description; no analytical method or data described
I065.summary_en: Describes a big data application system for college students' mental health based on a mobile internet platform to support mental health education. No analytical method, data or results are reported.

I066.summary_en: Predicts eustress and distress in about 800 college students aged 18–21 from a 28-item questionnaire validated by AIIMS Raipur experts, using Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, AdaBoost, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression and KNN. KNN reached 93% accuracy for eustress and Logistic Regression 99% for distress.

I067.screening_reason: Not about mental health; information dissemination and course selection platform
I067.summary_en: Builds an information dissemination model for a college students' network interaction platform, with course selection optimization and a parallel MapReduce sentiment analysis algorithm. No mental health outcome is addressed.

I068.screening_reason: Student management evaluation system; not about mental health
I068.summary_en: Designs an intelligent student management evaluation system based on SVM using teaching and student information, evaluated with experts at one university. No mental health outcome is addressed.

I069.summary_en: Summarizes prior studies using Random Forest classifiers to predict depression, anxiety and related problems in university students. It concludes that Random Forest is effective for early identification; no original data or results are reported.

I070.screening_reason: Student management data analysis; not about mental health
I070.summary_en: Analyzes data from an intelligent student management platform at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China to find associations among student behaviors, presenting four application cases. No mental health outcome is analyzed.

I071.screening_reason: English teaching data analysis; not about student mental health
I071.summary_en: Applies association rule mining to a college English teaching database to evaluate teaching effectiveness. No student mental health outcome is analyzed.

I072.summary_en: Compares Logistic Regression, SVM, KNN and Random Forest to predict students' mental health disorders from psychological, demographic and academic characteristics. Logistic Regression (F1 0.78) and Random Forest (F1 0.74) best balanced precision and recall; course and year of study were the most predictive factors.

I073.summary_en: Classifies academic and psychological challenges of 1,020 students at Jordanian universities from a validated electronic questionnaire, labeling categories with the GPT-4o mini LLM and evaluating machine learning classifiers. SVM performed best (88.2% accuracy); 60.8% of students reported psychological issues.

I074.screening_reason: Platform description focused mainly on physical health; no analytical method
I074.summary_en: Reviews physical and mental health problems of Chinese college students through literature analysis and proposes a big data and cloud-based digital health management platform with alert functions. No data analysis or results are reported.

I075.screening_reason: Information tracking system; no analytical method described
I075.summary_en: Proposes a college student mental health information tracking system (B/S and C/S, SSH, JSP) with Q&A and counseling appointment functions for monitoring students. No analytical method or results are reported.

I076.summary_en: Examines the relationship between anxiety, coping mechanisms, social anxiety and academic performance in first-year college students using correlation, t-tests and regression. Anxiety-related variables correlated negatively with academic performance, and coping mechanisms significantly influenced grades (t = −24.34).

I077.screening_reason: No data analytics applied; proposes crisis intervention strategies
I077.summary_en: Discusses online psychological evaluation using database and internet big data technology during COVID-19 and proposes crisis early warning, response and recovery mechanisms for universities. No data analysis is performed.

I078.screening_reason: General EDM/LA review; mental health is only one of many topics
I078.summary_en: Literature review comparing educational data mining and learning analytics techniques used to improve quality in higher education, mentioning mental health among other topics. No specific findings are reported.

I079.summary_en: Predicts stress in about 843 college students aged 18–21 from a 28-item questionnaire validated by AIIMS Raipur experts, comparing Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, AdaBoost, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression and KNN. SVM achieved the highest accuracy (95%).

I080.summary_en: Develops a ResNet model adapted to tabular data to classify student mental health using a Kaggle dataset with 20 features. Stratified k-fold cross-validation yielded about 95% accuracy.

I081.summary_en: Develops a web application that stores high school students' attendance and marks to predict entrance exam success and includes a mental health quiz analyzed with Random Forest. The model reached 94% accuracy; data size is not reported.

I082.screening_reason: Focus on physical fitness, not mental health
I082.summary_en: Builds BP neural network models of physical fitness for male and female undergraduates at one university using 2023 national physical health standard test data. The models showed high accuracy, with running tests and lung capacity as the main indicators.

I083.summary_en: Proposes an interpretable hybrid majority-vote framework (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest) to classify students' depression, anxiety and stress severity using DASS-21 and lifestyle variables, with feature rankings and if-then rules for counselors. No quantitative results are reported.

I084.screening_reason: Focus on curriculum design and academic performance; mental health only mentioned
I084.summary_en: Discusses how big data analytics can inform curriculum design and student performance in secondary education, mentioning mental health trends in passing. No data analysis or results are reported.

I085.screening_reason: Focus on physical health monitoring, not mental health
I085.summary_en: Discusses policies and the potential of big data for physical health monitoring of Chinese students and proposes integration strategies. No data analysis is performed.

I086.summary_en: Builds a pipeline with SMOTE, chi-square feature selection and PCA on the Kaggle Student Mental Health dataset, training Random Forest, Extra Trees, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, MLP and XGBoost. The tuned Decision Tree achieved the highest accuracy (99.05%).

I087.summary_en: Proposes OEDTL, an optimized explainable decision tree framework with novel preprocessing and dual-attention feature selection, applied to multi-source psychological, academic and behavioral data of 1,200 students to assign three risk levels. It achieves 98.78% accuracy, outperforming standard Decision Tree and Random Forest.

I088.best_result: Random Forest accuracy 95.28% (combined); Decision Tree accuracy 91.59% (junior high)
I088.summary_en: Develops a CRISP-DM predictive model of mental health risk with data from 426 junior and senior high school students (16 attributes) and a school prototype system. Random Forest performed best on senior high (95.07%) and combined data (95.28%), and Decision Tree on junior high data (91.59%).

I089.summary_en: Presents I-HOPE, an interpretable two-stage hierarchical model linking behavioral features to mental health status, evaluated on the five-year College Experience Study mobile sensing dataset. It achieves 91% accuracy versus 60–70% for baselines and provides individualized interpretable insights.

I090.best_result: BERT and custom NLP model accuracy 92%
I090.summary_en: Compares six NLP models (BERT, SVM, Random Forest, FLAN-T5, Mental-Llama and a custom model) to detect mental disorders using 10,000 textual responses from university students in Lima plus Reddit texts. BERT and the custom model achieved the highest accuracy (92%).

I091.screening_reason: Not about mental health; predicts graduate employment rate
I091.best_result: BP neural network minimum absolute error 0.154
I091.summary_en: Simulates a three-layer BP neural network to predict college graduates' employment rate using 2015–2021 employment data. The minimum absolute error was 0.154.

I092.summary_en: Builds a big data-based monitoring and early warning model for the mental health of international students in China using multi-source data fusion, feature extraction and LSTM analysis of temporal data. It reports application in practical cases without metrics.

I093.summary_en: Synthesizes 25 peer-reviewed studies on AI techniques for student mental health risk prediction and proposes FEMHA, a federated, explainable and SDG-aligned framework. It identifies trends, challenges and research gaps without empirical testing.

I094.summary_en: Compares Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Naive Bayes and SVM with grid search, Bayesian and particle swarm hyperparameter optimization to classify college students' mental health from SCL-90 assessment data. PSO-optimized LightGBM performed best (F1 0.9790, AUC 0.9945).

I095.summary_en: Compares reinforcement learning (250 samples) with KNN (200 samples) for predicting students' mental health. Reinforcement learning reached 85–94% accuracy versus 72–81% for KNN.

I096.screening_reason: General educational analytics essay; mental health is not the focus
I096.summary_en: Discusses the use of data analytics for holistic student development, including personalized learning, dashboards and tracking of socio-emotional learning. No data analysis or results are reported.

I097.screening_reason: Population not specifically students (students and working professionals)
I097.summary_en: Develops a mental health app with smartwatch integration that sends real-time health data to an AI backend using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting for stress assessment, targeting students and working professionals. No data or metrics are reported.

I098.summary_en: Establishes an emotional analysis model and platform for college students' public opinion information based on big data to support monitoring and crisis warning. No data or results are reported.

I099.summary_en: Evaluates an 8-week positive psychology group counseling intervention in vocational college freshmen (experimental vs control classes) using SWLS, GWB and APAS scales, and predicts intervention effect with Logistic Regression, SVM and Random Forest. Random Forest performed best; general well-being and life satisfaction were the key features.

I100.summary_en: Conducts a large-scale empirical study of mental health forecasting using the multi-year College Experience Study with passive smartphone sensing and weekly surveys, comparing model granularity and architecture choices. Population-level models achieved the highest forecasting accuracy (up to 0.777), while personalization and two-stage pipelines gave limited or negative gains.

I101.summary_en: Discusses secondary psychological counseling stations in the Internet+ era and applies mean clustering and C4.5 to college students' mental health big data to identify factors leading to mental health problems. No data details or results are reported.

I102.summary_en: Develops a probabilistic predictive model within a decision support system to identify university students' depression, anxiety and stress. Accuracy was 59.14% for depression, 56.67% for anxiety and 63.70% for stress; the data are not described.

I103.best_result: Fine-tuned BERT 96% (journals); Random Forest accuracy 90%, F1 0.90
I103.summary_en: Presents MindSync, a platform analyzing surveys, journals and voice recordings with a Random Forest risk classifier trained on 621 student records and a fine-tuned BERT for journal entries. Random Forest reached 90% accuracy and BERT 96% across metrics; moderate- and high-risk students are flagged for counselors.

I104.summary_en: Predicts student depression from 27,901 records with 18 demographic, academic, lifestyle and psychosocial features, using SMOTE-Tomek, chi-square selection, six tree-based classifiers and a stacking ensemble. CatBoost achieved the best cross-validated performance (87.23% accuracy, 87.62% F1).

I105.best_result: Accuracy up to 99%, recall up to 99%
I105.summary_en: Designs a student psychological assessment and counseling system based on unspecified data mining algorithms, validated through simulation and performance experiments. Accuracy exceeded 90% and recall 80%, reaching up to 99%, without describing the data.

I106.summary_en: Proposes graph representation learning to predict the mental well-being of 20 undergraduate and graduate students from questionnaire and ECG data collected during four weeks of robot-assisted journaling with Pepper. It achieved 92.5% accuracy, outperforming standard ML methods.

I107.screening_reason: Focus on physical fitness monitoring, not mental health
I107.summary_en: Constructs a neural network-based model for monitoring college students' physical fitness from physical test data. No mental health outcome is analyzed.

I108.summary_en: Proposes an AI-powered mobile companion combining safety features (SOS, geolocation) with NLP-based emotion detection from students' journaling and interaction patterns. A preliminary evaluation reports reduced emergency response delays and greater engagement without quantitative detail.

I109.screening_reason: Focus on physical health test data, not mental health
I109.summary_en: Applies FP-Growth association rule mining to physical health test data from six universities to analyze Chinese college students' physique. The method is reported to have reference value for system design.

I110.screening_reason: Outcome is cosmetic surgery acceptance; conventional statistical survey analysis
I110.summary_en: Examines the relationship between cosmetic surgery acceptance, objectified body consciousness and stress in 301 South Asian medical students in Shandong, China, using validated scales and mediation analysis. Acceptance correlated with stress (r = 0.175) and body consciousness (r = 0.181), which partially mediated the stress effect.

I111.summary_en: Introduces an AI therapist conversational agent (Autogen) for college students that applies sentiment analysis to conversations and visualizes emotional trends over time. No data or evaluation results are reported.

I112.summary_en: Uses Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost and CatBoost to identify academic, social and lifestyle factors associated with university students' depression, anxiety and future insecurity. Lifestyle, workload and negative campus experiences were related to mental health; no metrics are reported.

I113.summary_en: Proposes RRP-C4.5, combining ReliefF feature selection, a C4.5 decision tree and reduced error pruning, to classify university students' mental health conditions from a student mental health assessment dataset. It achieved 98.43% accuracy, above the standard C4.5.

I114.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; stress used only as a predictor
I114.summary_en: Predicts college students' academic performance from sleep, study habits, stress and lifestyle using Linear Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost and a DNN. XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy (0.90) and Linear Regression R² 0.85 for GPA; study hours, sleep and motivation were the main predictors.

I115.screening_reason: Outcome is effectiveness of counseling data rather than students' mental health; data not described
I115.summary_en: Proposes a deep learning model to assess the effectiveness of university student psychological counseling data and compares it with a decision tree. The deep learning model outperformed the decision tree in accuracy, efficiency and stability without reported figures.

I116.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; no data or results; refers to patients rather than students
I116.summary_en: Discusses the application of the ID3 decision tree algorithm in college mental health education to identify depression, anxiety and stress. The abstract is incoherent and reports no data or results.

I117.screening_reason: Focus on student dropout, not mental health
I117.summary_en: Proposes a software framework that predicts student dropout risk from engagement, performance, behavior and socio-economic indicators using Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression, with intervention recommendations. No results are reported.
